preview.headline: USA's run game meets the Sun Belt's hottest defense.
preview.summary: Louisiana Tech arrives 3-0 in the Sun Belt with two straight shutouts; South Alabama is home after an 11-day break and a 13-point night at Marshall.

matchup.why: Close on paper, but Tech's average includes 80 against FCS Northwestern State; it has scored 24 to 32 in each of its last four.
Tech has shut out ULM (24-0) and Old Dominion (26-0) in its last two games.
The biggest gap on the page. USA allows 414.6 yards a game; Tech allows 323.4.
USA's best weapon. Old Dominion ran for minus-12 yards against Tech last week, so this is a real test.
Blake Baker went 28-of-34 for 303 yards last week; USA's pass defense has been its weak spot.
USA's clearest statistical edge, and the one that went missing at Marshall (lost it 1-0).
USA went 4-of-18 on third down at Marshall; Tech's defense has 19 sacks to make third-and-long worse.

usa: Run the ball and stay on schedule. USA averages 214.3 rushing yards; Keenan Phillips ran for 284 yards and four TDs at Arkansas State.
Protect Hollins on third down. Tech has 19 sacks, 6.5 by Alonzo Jackson Jr., and USA converted 4 of 18 third downs at Marshall.
Win the turnover battle. USA is +5 on the year; Tech has 8 giveaways.
opp: Let Baker throw. He averages 8.1 yards a pass and USA allows 252.9 passing yards a game.
Make USA one-dimensional. Tech's front held Old Dominion to minus-12 rushing yards; stopping Phillips early forces Hollins into long third downs.

players.name: Keenan Phillips
players.note: 96 carries, 514 yards, 5 TD. Held to 70 yards on 16 carries at Marshall; 4+ yards a carry here means USA's line is winning.

players.name: Jared Hollins
players.note: 68-of-125, 1,003 yards, 7 TD, 3 INT. Was 12-of-33 for 148 yards at Marshall; watch his completion rate against Tech's pass rush.

players.name: Blake Baker
players.note: 96-of-133 (72%), 1,160 yards, 10 TD, 1 INT. Threw for 303 and ran for a TD against Old Dominion.

players.name: Alonzo Jackson Jr.
players.note: Tech's leader in sacks (6.5) and tackles (48). The player most likely to stall USA drives on passing downs.

watch.title: USA's first two drives
watch.text: The offense scored 13 at Marshall and has had 11 days to fix it. Early points at home would test a Tech defense that has not allowed one in eight quarters.

watch.title: Jalen Mickens and Eli Finley vs. USA's secondary
watch.text: Mickens leads Tech with 40 catches for 586 yards; Finley had 10 catches for 128 yards last week. Long completions here are the clearest danger sign.

watch.title: A close finish
watch.text: Tech beat Army 31-29 and Louisiana 32-31. USA lost its last game on a touchdown drive with 1:49 left. Late-game execution may decide it.

injuries: No injury report found for either team as of Oct 29.
QB Bishop Davenport started Week 1; Jared Hollins has started since the Ohio game on Sept 19. Davenport's status: not found.
preview.weather: ESPN/AccuWeather forecast for kickoff (checked Oct 29): 77°F, 49% chance of rain, gusts to 13 mph.

lastGame.usa: Lost 20-13 at Marshall on Oct 20 (4-of-18 on third down, one interception).
lastGame.opp: Beat Old Dominion 26-0 on Oct 24, its second straight shutout and fourth straight win.

prediction.reasoning: Tech's defense allows nearly two yards a play less than USA's, and its passing game lines up against USA's weakest unit. USA has home field, extra rest, the better run game and the better turnover margin, which keeps this a one-score game.
prediction.risks: Tech's shutouts came against ULM and an Old Dominion team starting its third-string QB. If Phillips runs like he did at Arkansas State and USA wins the turnover battle again, the Jaguars can win comfortably at home.

preview.context: Louisiana Tech leads the series 2-1; USA won the last meeting 38-14 in Mobile in 2022. First meeting as Sun Belt opponents (Tech joined the league this season from Conference USA). Tech leads the West at 3-0; USA is 2-1, so the winner has the inside track. Military Appreciation Day at Hancock Whitney Stadium. Kickoff 2 p.m. Central.

notes: Injuries: still no injury report found for either team (ESPN game page, checked 8:30 a.m. game day). Starting QB status unchanged from the preview: Hollins has started since Sept 19; Davenport not found.

Weather has warmed since the preview. ESPN/AccuWeather now shows 82°F at kickoff, 46% chance of rain and gusts to 17 mph (was 77°F, 49%, 13 mph). FOX10 forecasts about 80°F in the first half, upper 70s by the fourth quarter, mostly sun and clouds with only a small risk of a brief shower; rain chances rise after dark.
Kickoff is still 2 p.m. Central on ESPN+ at Hancock Whitney Stadium. No new South Alabama or Louisiana Tech news found since the preview, so the pick stays USA 24, LT 27 (Low confidence).

grade.summary: The brief picked Louisiana Tech 27-24 and Tech won 35-20, so the winner and total were close but the margin was off by 12. It was right that Baker and Tech’s passing game would beat USA’s secondary and that USA’s run game would work, but it missed how costly USA’s two turnovers, 12 penalties and second-half shutout would be.

keys.key: USA: Run the ball and stay on schedule.
keys.note: 44 carries for 205 yards (4.7 a carry), well above the 125.4 Tech had allowed a game; PJ Martin ran for 82 and Phillips for 62 and a TD. The run game did not carry into points after halftime.

keys.key: USA: Protect Hollins on third down.
keys.note: 6 of 14 on third down (43%), up from 4 of 18 at Marshall; Tech was credited with 1.5 sacks (Taeden Rogers 1, Alonzo Jackson Jr. 0.5).
Lost it 2-0. Phillips fumbled at the USA 6 late in the third quarter, setting up Tech’s last TD, and Hollins was intercepted at the Tech 5 with 1:40 left.
Baker went 10 of 16 for 167 yards and 3 TDs; Tech averaged 11.4 yards a pass and scored TDs on four straight first-half drives.
USA ran for 205 yards and outgained Tech 397 to 315; Tech won with turnovers, red-zone stops and fourth-down stops instead.

players.name: Keenan Phillips
players.note: 11 carries, 62 yards (5.6 a carry), 11-yard TD run; 2 kick returns for 68 yards. Lost a fumble at the USA 6 that led to a Tech TD. PJ Martin led USA with 82 yards on 12 carries.

players.name: Jared Hollins
players.note: 14 of 31 (45%), 192 yards, 2 TD to Anthony Eager (7 catches, 102 yards), 1 INT at the Tech 5 on the last drive; also 14 carries for 38 yards.

players.name: Blake Baker
players.note: 10 of 16, 167 yards, 3 TD, 0 INT; 16 carries for 35 yards. Backup Trey Kukuk added a 27-yard TD pass to Jalen Mickens.

players.name: Alonzo Jackson Jr.
players.note: Led Tech with 9 tackles, 0.5 sack and recovered Phillips’ fumble at the USA 6.

grade.missed: It expected a one-score game decided late; Tech led by 15 after three quarters and nobody scored in the fourth. It counted on USA’s +5 turnover margin and did not flag penalties: USA had 12 for 100 yards, went 1 of 4 on fourth down, missed an extra point and was shut out after halftime despite 397 total yards. Marcus Calwise Jr. (3 catches, 68 yards, 2 TD) and Rayshun Hurt (67-yard catch) were the big-play receivers, not Finley.

performance.summary: A 15-point home loss to the West Division leader. USA outgained Tech 397 to 315 with 24 first downs and 205 rushing yards, and the defense allowed only one TD after halftime, on a 10-yard field after a fumble. But Tech scored TDs on four straight first-half drives (11.4 yards a pass), and USA beat itself with 2 turnovers, 12 penalties for 100 yards, 1-of-4 on fourth down, a missed PAT and zero second-half points.

accuracy.note: Picked Tech by 3; Tech won by 15, off by 12.
Picked 51 points; the game had 55, off by 4.
3 of 5 keys held up; USA lost the turnover battle and was not made one-dimensional.
Baker, Jackson Jr. and the danger of long Tech completions were right, and USA did score on its first two drives; the close finish did not happen and Calwise, not Finley, did the damage.

fixes.title: Penalties
fixes.text: 12 penalties for 100 yards, against 4 for 29 by Tech. That is too many flags to win on the road at Louisiana on Nov 7.

fixes.title: Ball security near the goal lines
fixes.text: Phillips’ fumble at the USA 6 handed Tech a 10-yard TD drive, and Hollins’ interception at the Tech 5 ended the last real chance. Two turnovers in the red zones cost up to 14 points.

fixes.title: Turn yards into second-half points
fixes.text: 397 yards but 0 points after halftime; three drives ended on downs (1 of 4 on fourth down) and three in punts. Pick better fourth-down calls or take points when they are there.

fixes.title: Deep pass defense
fixes.text: Tech completed 11 of 17 for 194 yards (11.4 a pass) with TDs of 22, 27 and 35 yards and a 67-yard catch, scoring on four straight first-half drives. Safeties have to keep the ball in front.

fixes.title: Hollins’ accuracy
fixes.text: 14 of 31 (45%) after 12 of 33 at Marshall. Two straight games under 50% puts the offense behind schedule; more quick throws off the run game.
